I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over thirty years. My family has about 8 mu. I know what I'm doing — wheat in the winter, corn in the summer. That's how it works here, that's what my neighbors do, and that's what the soil and water here are suited for.

**Winter wheat** goes in this October. I'll go to the village cooperative to buy certified seed — the improved varieties they sell there yield better than keeping my own seed. I apply base fertilizer before planting, mostly compound fertilizer, and then top-dress with urea at jointing. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, at heading, and once more during grain filling — four times. The wheat needs it; we don't get enough rain. I spray herbicide in spring and fungicide when powdery mildew shows up. I'll rotary-till the field after the corn comes off in autumn to prepare for wheat planting.

**Summer maize** goes straight in after wheat harvest in June — I don't plow, just direct-seed into the stubble. I always buy hybrid seed; you can't save that kind, but the yields are good. Summer rains here usually handle most of the water need — I'll only irrigate once if July is dry. I apply fertilizer at planting and again at the big bell stage. I spray once for pests, maybe twice if the armyworm shows up badly.

I'm not trying anything new this year. At my age, with 8 mu to manage mostly by myself, I stick with what I know works.
